newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bulls rampant as German shares keep up record run.
newsitem.headline: Bulls rampant as German shares keep up record run.

text.p: Bulls ran rampant in electronic share trade in Frankfurt on Friday afternoon as the dollar penetrated the 1.67-mark threshold and the Dow Jones Industrial index opened sharply higher to underpin lively IBIS DAX trade.

The German electronic IBIS DAX index continued its record-breaking run to stand at 3,161.90 points, up 37.12 points early on,just off a high of 3,165.27 with no bearish signs in sight to stymie the seemingly-unstoppable advance.
"Just look at the dollar - we've been through 1.67 marks and are now above that, U.S. non-farm payroll data was good and Wall Street is up -- a classic bull market," said one trader.
"It could be that everything looks a little bit exaggerated right now and it won't look so rosy on Monday morning. But we are still in liquidity markets, markets that want to go up," said the trader.
"While all the ingredients are there to go higher, we have to go higher," said the trader.

If Wall Street stays higher, the dollar stays around current levels and the G7 meeting of finance ministers in Berlin at the weekend does not produce any unexpected findings, dealers are expecting more of the same for next week.
One possible downside is Germany's Fasching holiday.
The annual regional holiday, which started on Thursday, has a greater impact in northern Germany and does not affect Frankfurt until Tuesday when markets close for the afternoon.
Dealers said that volumes might be muted, but that in its current position there was no real reason to suspect any major impact on the trend and for volumes to contract significantly.

Volume leader in afternoon trade was electronics group Siemens AG, which started its rise after breaking an important technical barrier at 81 marks, and continued its rise boosted by a mixture of positive fundamental factors and an element of market rumour.
Market speculation about a possible restructuring by Siemens, which traders said could be announced next week, drove the share higher on Thursday which continued on Friday morning.

In afternoon electronic trade Siemens stood at 86.25 marks, up 92 pfennigs, off earlier highs of 86.34 marks. The share's rise on Friday started with news it had won an order to supply equipment for the German D2 mobile phone system operated by Mannesmann Mobilfunk.
Bayerische Vereinsbank and Dresdner Bank also raised their rating of Siemens shares, which helped lift the share price.
"We are seeing a lot of sector rotation at the moment -- banks, chemicals -- today it's second-liners," said a trader.
The chemical sector saw considerable volumes, with the high dollar, with BASF AG up 48 pfennigs at 61.83 marks, Bayer AG up 63 pfennigs at 65.94 marks and Hoechst AG up 49 pfennigs at 72.78 marks.
Veba AG was up 25 pfennigs at 92.20 marks, off earlier highs, after C&W withdrew from a telecoms alliance and a seperate telecoms deal with RWE received cartel office approval.
